1. Früh und regelmäßig etwas Nützliches:
1. Deliver something useful early and regularly – that satisfies customers best.
2. Changing requirements are welcome, even late.
3. Deliver working results at short intervals, weeks rather than months.
4. Business people and developers work together daily.
5. Build projects around motivated people; give them the environment, support and trust they need.
6. Face-to-face conversation is the best way to share information.
7. Progress is measured by what works.
8. Keep a pace everyone can sustain indefinitely.
9. Technical quality and good design keep you agile.
10. Simplicity: maximise the amount of work not done.
11. Good solutions emerge from self-organising teams.
12. Pause regularly, improve together and adjust the way you work.

Ein Board zeigt den Arbeitsfluss auf ein:
A board shows the flow of work at a glance: columns such as “Open – In progress – Done”, every card a small, self-contained piece of work. This is how the four values fit in:
• Individuals and interactions: share boards, assign cards and bring people into the conversation with @-mentions – LiNotes supports the conversation but doesn’t replace it.
• Working software: cut cards small and only move them to “Done” when it really works; in development projects evidence proves it.
• Customer collaboration: invite your client to the board: they write wishes as cards and accept them themselves – e.g. agreed so that only they move cards to “Done”.
• Responding to change: change priorities and reorder cards at any time; plans show postponed milestones openly instead of hiding them.

Reflect regularly: create the report as a PDF and go through it together – what went well, what do we change? Documentation only as much as necessary: impact analysis, verification and evidence are meant for projects that need them (e.g. under ISO 26262 or Automotive SPICE) – simple boards stay lean.

Manifest für Agile Softwareentwicklung\n:
Manifesto for Agile Software Development

We are uncovering better ways of developing software by doing it and helping others do it. Through this work we have come to value:

Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Working software over comprehensive documentation
Customer collaboration over contract negotiation
Responding to change over following a plan

That is, while there is value in the items on the right, we value the items on the left more.

Kent Beck, Mike Beedle, Arie van Bennekum, Alistair Cockburn, Ward Cunningham, Martin Fowler, James Grenning, Jim Highsmith, Andrew Hunt, Ron Jeffries, Jon Kern, Brian Marick, Robert C. Martin, Steve Mellor, Ken Schwaber, Jeff Sutherland, Dave Thomas
